Name: Better auto-grabber
Author: Milaz21
Description:
[size=5][b]Better Auto-Grabber[/b][/size]

Auto-grabbers collect animal products from the building they stand in, and nothing else, ever. This mod gives every placed grabber its own settings: [b]what[/b] it collects, [b]where[/b] it reaches, and [b]how often[/b] it runs.

One grabber outside can now serve every coop and barn on the farm. Wake up, walk to it, and the eggs, milk, wool and last night's truffles are already inside.

Vanilla behaviour is untouched. A grabber with nothing ticked behaves exactly like a stock one: dropped in a coop it still collects that coop's eggs, and it still does nothing anywhere else. You opt in, one grabber at a time.

[b]It can collect:[/b] forage, crops (including indoor pots), fruit trees, bushes (including ones in garden pots), large stumps and logs, boulders and meteorites, ore and gem nodes, rocks, twigs and weeds, artifact and seed spots, panning spots, tree shaking, tree moss, trash cans, animal products, machines, and buildings that hold finished goods for you: fish ponds and mills.

[b]Modded content works out of the box[/b], with nothing extra to install: crops, fruit, forage, animals, machines and bushes added by other mods are collectable too.
[line]

[size=4][b]How to use it[/b][/size]

Right-click a grabber to open it, including an empty one, which vanilla refuses to open, and click the [b]![/b] button on the right edge of the menu. Three tabs: [b]What to grab[/b], [b]Where from[/b], and [b]How it runs[/b].

Settings are stored on the grabber itself. They save with your game, survive being picked up and put back down, and stay attached to the right grabber when you own several.

[b]The three tabs in full:[/b]
[spoiler]
[b]What to grab[/b] is a searchable list of everything the grabber may take, with each row showing what the grabber actually interacts with. Forage, crops and fruit are listed as the item itself. A large log is listed as the log, because "hardwood" doesn't tell you where it should come from. Machines are listed by machine. Nothing is ticked by default. Searching matches row names and group names, so typing "animal" lists the whole Animals group rather than nothing.

[b]Everything else here[/b] is the first row of most groups, and it stands for the part of that group the list can't show you: forage the game drops from its own code, a crop whose harvest is decided as it is picked, a machine another mod adds that the game's own data never names. It is a row like any other and it speaks only for itself. Ticking it does not tick anything below it, and the rows below it are collected only when you tick them, so what you see ticked is exactly what the grabber takes.

[b]Check all[/b] on a group's heading ticks the rows you can see and leaves [b]Everything else here[/b] alone, so "every crop in the game right now, but not whatever a mod adds next month" is a single click. Neither one moves the other, in either direction. Searching narrows what check all acts on, so it ticks what is in front of you rather than the whole group. Groups whose rows are fixed and few (stumps and boulders, digging, trees, trash cans) have no "everything else" row at all, because nothing can turn up in them that the list wouldn't already show.

[b]Where from[/b] sets the grabber's reach:
[list]
[*][b]This location only[/b], the location the grabber stands in[/*]
[*][b]Everywhere I've been[/b], every location you've visited at least once[/*]
[*][b]Chosen locations[/b], only the ones you tick[/*]
[/list]There is one row per kind of building, and ticking it reaches all of them. A single [b]Coop[/b] row covers every coop you own, both of them if you have two, and whatever their tier, since a Coop, a Big Coop and a Deluxe Coop are all just coops. Barns, sheds and cabins work the same way. The rows follow each building's upgrade chain, so a coop tier added by a content pack joins the Coop row on its own. There is no way to serve one coop and leave the one beside it alone: the game gives building interiors a unique ID but no name a player would recognise, so a row per building would have to be labelled [i]Coop4cb0a4d1-3f8b-49c9-a375-eb8251426524[/i].

Everywhere else is listed under the name players actually use for it. The game names a location only where its own data says so, and it says nothing for most of the map, so the list would otherwise read [i]BugLand[/i], [i]Club[/i], [i]SkullCave[/i] and [i]IslandWest[/i] instead of Mutant Bug Lair, Casino, Skull Cavern and Ginger Island West. Where the game does name a place that name is kept, since it is the canonical one and is already translated. The internal name stays beside each row, because it is what tells the farm, the farmhouse and the cellar apart.

The Quarry isn't on the list: it is part of the Mountain map rather than a location of its own, so a grabber that reaches the Mountain already reaches the quarry.

[b]How it runs[/b] is the third tab, holding the two settings that are about neither what nor where.

[b]Runs[/b] sets how often this grabber works (every 10 minutes, hourly, every 4 hours, or once a day) or leaves it following the mod-wide default. Every grabber also runs once as the day begins whatever its interval, so you never walk past an empty grabber on your way out of the house.

It runs at two other moments regardless of its interval: when you close its settings page, and when you put down a grabber that already has rows ticked. Otherwise the first pass after ticking a row would be whenever the interval next came round, the next whole hour by default, and not until tomorrow morning on a daily one, which reads a lot like nothing happened.

[b]Replant crops[/b] decides what a grabber puts back in the soil it just harvested, using only seeds kept in the grabber itself: [i]never[/i] (the default), [i]with matching seed[/i], or [i]with any seed[/i]. The crop's own seed is always tried first, so [i]with any seed[/i] is about keeping soil in use once the right seed runs out, not about turning a parsnip field into whatever else was in the box. A seed is only planted where you could have planted it yourself: right season, right location, and only into empty soil.[/spoiler]
[line]

[size=4][b]What it can collect[/b][/size]

Tree shaking runs the game's own shake, so it yields whatever shaking by hand would: seeds, the occasional mystery box, and anything a content pack adds. Machines go through the game's own collection path, so crystalariums restart, tappers reload, and harvest stats and skill experience are credited as normal.

[b]Harvest moss[/b] is a separate row in the [b]Trees[/b] group, and it carries the same price cutting moss by hand does: the tree drops back several growth stages, and the moss only returns once it has grown all the way back. Leave the row unticked if you would rather keep your trees where they are. No scythe needed, since every farm has one and no upgrade to it changes what the cut gives.

The [b]Forage[/b] group also lists the things the game drops on the ground from its own code rather than from a data file: coral, sea urchins and seaweed on the beach, on Ginger Island's west shore and in the dangerous mines, and magma caps and dragon teeth on the volcano floors. Spring onions and ginger are listed under Crops, since they grow in soil rather than lying on the ground. Ginger is dug rather than picked, so it needs a hoe on the same terms as an artifact spot.

Three deliberate omissions:
[list]
[*][b]Giant crops[/b] are never harvested. Plenty of people grow them as decoration, and felling one is destructive in a way nothing else on the list is.[/*]
[*][b]Golden walnut bushes[/b] aren't collectable.[/*]
[*][b]Incubators[/b] are never emptied. What one holds is the egg you gave it, and it reports itself ready on the morning the timer runs out, before you get to the coop and the chick hatches. Taking it would hand the egg back and cancel the hatch, so incubators are left off the list entirely.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Rocks and litter[/b], ore nodes and everything else breakable:
[spoiler]
Every node on the wiki's mining table has a row: copper, iron, gold, iridium and radioactive, the seven gem nodes, gem and mystic stones, all four geodes, cinder shard, fossil, clay, mussel, calico egg and coal. Plain stone, snowy stone, twigs and weeds are listed too, each on its own row, so clearing clutter and mining ore stay separate decisions.

Breaking a node runs the game's own code, so what comes out is whatever your own pickaxe would have got on that tile that day, down to the Prospector's extra coal and the Mystic Stone's prismatic shard. Mining experience and the rocks crushed stat are credited as normal.

The game's names are kept, which is why the fossil node the wiki calls a Bone Node is listed as [b]Fossil Stone[/b]. The one exception is the coal node, which the game calls "Stone" like any grey rock; with no name of its own it would have been buried in the Stone row, so this mod names it.

Rows follow vanilla's tool rules. Any pickaxe breaks any rock except an Emerald Stone, which needs steel or better, and an Aquamarine Stone, which needs copper or better. Twigs need an axe. Weeds need nothing worth checking.

Worth knowing before you tick these: [b]the Quarry is part of the Mountain map[/b], so a grabber that reaches the Mountain clears the quarry's nodes, iridium included, on every pass.[/spoiler]

[b]Panning spots[/b], the glittering spot in the water:
[spoiler]
[b]Panning Spot[/b] sits in the [b]Digging[/b] group, and covers the glittering spot that appears in a location's water once the Fish Tank bundle is done. A grabber reaching that location works it with a pan and drops the haul in the box, sparkle and all.

The loot is the game's own roll, so your luck, your pan's upgrade level and any enchantment on it all count. So does the upgrade's other perk: a steel pan or better rolls for a fresh spot the moment the old one is worked, exactly as it does when you pan by hand.

You never have to carry the pan, and it can stay on your head. Most people wear theirs as a hat, which is where the ownership check looks first.[/spoiler]

[b]Trash cans[/b], and the one thing to know before ticking them:
[spoiler]
The [b]Trash Cans[/b] group is one row, and it rummages every trash can in the locations the grabber reaches: the eight around town, plus any a content pack has added, since they're found by reading the map rather than from a list. There's no row per can: the game's own IDs for them are internal handles like [i]JodiAndKent[/i], and which cans a grabber reaches is the scope tab's job anyway. A grabber sitting on the farm won't touch them; one set to [i]Everywhere I've been[/i], or with Town ticked under [i]Chosen locations[/i], will.

Worth knowing before you tick it: [b]a can can only be searched once a day, by anyone.[/b] This is the one target that takes something off your own to-do list. If a grabber gets to the cans first, they're empty when you walk past. The roll is the game's own, so daily luck and the Trash Book still apply, and what would have come out is what lands in the grabber.

Nobody gets upset about it, either. Searching a can by hand costs you 25 friendship with whoever is standing nearby and gets announced in chat; a grabber doesn't make the walk and isn't seen doing it, the same reasoning that keeps milking from earning friendship.[/spoiler]

[b]Buildings[/b], the fish pond and the mill:
[spoiler]
The [b]Buildings[/b] group covers the things that hold finished goods for you but aren't objects on the map. Nothing in this group could be collected before, whatever the grabber was set up to do: a building isn't an object standing on a tile, so no pass ever saw one.

[b]Fish Pond[/b] takes whatever is waiting in the pond's bucket: roe, and the ink, algae and fish some ponds give instead. Fishing experience is credited exactly as collecting by hand credits it, scaled by what the produce is worth. It never feeds a pond, so one asking for an item to raise its population goes on asking: handing over five cinder shards is your call to make, not a grabber's.

[b]Mill[/b] empties the flour hopper. Nothing else about the mill changes: what it grinds next is decided at the start of the day from whatever is in its input chest, which the grabber never touches. Putting wheat [i]in[/i] is still your job.

Rows are built from the game's own building data, so a building a content pack adds is listed the day you install it, as long as its data says where the finished goods end up. A chest the building takes its inputs from is never emptied, for the obvious reason.

One deliberate omission: [b]junimo huts aren't collectable[/b]. A hut's chest is the junimos' own drop-off and plenty of people keep things in it, which makes it storage rather than an output hopper. Emptying it would be taking from a chest you fill.

A full grabber leaves a building alone rather than dropping what doesn't fit on the ground: the goods stay in the hopper, or in the pond, until there's room.[/spoiler]

[b]Animal products[/b], reach rather than capability:
[spoiler]
The [b]Animals[/b] group lists every item a farm animal produces, one row per item. Egg and Large Egg are separate rows, so ticking one doesn't quietly give you the other. Rows are built from the game's own animal data, so animals added by content packs appear on their own. Slime balls share the group: they aren't animal produce, but clearing a hutch is the same chore.

The point of the group is reach. A stock grabber only serves the building it stands in; one grabber outside with the right scope serves every coop and barn you own, and picks up truffles from the farm during the day as the pigs dig them.

[b]It obeys the scope tab like everything else.[/b] A grabber on the farm set to [i]This location only[/i] reaches the farm, truffles and any animal that has wandered out to graze, but not the inside of a coop. To collect eggs, milk and wool you have to tick [b]Coop[/b] and [b]Barn[/b] under [i]Chosen locations[/i], or use [i]Everywhere I've been[/i].

Two things it deliberately doesn't do:
[list]
[*][b]No friendship.[/b] Milking by hand gives friendship for the walk over; a grabber didn't make the walk. If you want your animals to love you faster, pet them.[/*]
[*][b]A pig's truffle stays on the pig[/b] until the pig digs it up outdoors, in season, in fair weather. Taking it straight off the animal would be a guaranteed truffle a day from a pig that never left the barn.[/*]
[/list]Milk and wool need no milk pail or shears. A stock grabber standing in a barn already collects them without either, so requiring one here would be stricter than the game is with itself.[/spoiler]

[b]Content from other mods[/b], and why it just works:
[spoiler]
Nothing extra to install, and nothing to configure. Rows are built from the game's own data at load time, so crops, fruit, forage, animals and machines added by a content pack are on the list the first time you open a grabber after installing it.

Bushes are the exception, because the game has no data file for them: what a bush gives is decided in code, which is why mods that add bushes do it by changing what an existing bush answers. This mod asks the bush rather than assuming, so a modded bush is collected correctly, pays out the stack and quality its pack intended, and gets a row of its own named after what it gives once one has been seen growing in your save, from the next morning. Until a row exists, [b]Everything else here[/b] under Bushes is what collects it.

That is the general rule: anything this mod cannot name is collectable through its group's [b]Everything else here[/b] row the day the mod adding it is installed. Anything it can name gets a row instead, and a row is yours to tick, including one that appears later, which starts out unticked like every other.[/spoiler]
[line]

[size=4][b]Several grabbers[/b][/size]

Grabbers never take the same item twice. Whichever runs first removes it from the world and the next one finds nothing there, so overlapping reaches are safe. When two grabbers want the same thing, the one with the narrower scope gets first pick: a grabber watching one location beats one sweeping half the valley.
[line]

[size=4][b]Working with Automate[/b][/size]

Both mods can collect from machines, and [b]Automate will almost always win[/b]. It polls constantly while a grabber runs at most every ten in-game minutes, so any machine wired into an Automate network is emptied by Automate first. Nothing breaks, the output still reaches a chest, but two things are worth knowing:
[spoiler]
[list]
[*]Machines drained by Automate stop paying [b]skill experience[/b], which this mod grants when it collects them itself.[/*]
[*]The overlap only exists where you have already built a network. A tapper out in the woods with no chest beside it is exactly what a grabber is for.[/*]
[/list]The pairing that makes both mods worth having: let the [b]grabber collect[/b] from what Automate can't reach, and let [b]Automate drain the grabber[/b] into your storage. That works today, a grabber's container is deliberately left as a plain chest so Automate keeps recognising it.

If a machine is already handled by your Automate network, just don't tick it.[/spoiler]
[line]

[size=4][b]Configuration[/b][/size]

Edit [b]config.json[/b] or use [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url].
[spoiler]
[list]
[*][b]DefaultFrequency[/b] ([i]Hourly[/i]), how often grabbers run unless one overrides it[/*]
[*][b]RespectToolRequirements[/b] ([i]true[/i]), large stumps need a copper axe, logs a steel axe, and so on (see below)[/*]
[*][b]GrantExperience[/b] ([i]true[/i]), grant the skill experience harvesting by hand would give[/*]
[*][b]SkipFestivalLocations[/b] ([i]true[/i]), leave festival and event maps alone[/*]
[*][b]DailySummary[/b] ([i]true[/i]), report each day what the grabbers collected[/*]
[*][b]VerboseLogging[/b] ([i]false[/i]), log every pass in detail[/*]
[*][b]SettingsButtonOffsetX / Y[/b] ([i]0[/i]), nudge the [b]![/b] button if another mod's button overlaps it[/*]
[/list]
[b]Tool requirements[/b]

With [b]RespectToolRequirements[/b] on, a grabber only takes what your tools could handle: a copper axe for large stumps, a steel axe for hollow logs, a steel pickaxe for boulders, a gold pickaxe for meteorites, any pickaxe for rocks and ore nodes (a steel one for emerald nodes, a copper one for aquamarine nodes), any axe for twigs, any hoe for artifact and seed spots and for digging ginger, any pan for panning spots.

It counts a tool you [b]own[/b], not one you carry. The world is checked once a day, so a pickaxe left in a chest at home counts, and so does the tool sitting at Clint's forge during the two days of an upgrade, when it belongs to no inventory at all. A pan worn as a hat counts as a pan. Picking up a finished upgrade counts straight away.

Because the game never records the level a tool was upgraded to, the best of each kind seen is remembered in your save: once you have owned a gold pickaxe, your grabbers keep mining meteorites even if that pickaxe is later lost or thrown away.[/spoiler]
[line]

[size=4][b]Install[/b][/size]

[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://smapi.io]SMAPI[/url] 4.0.0 or newer.[/*]
[*]Unzip into your [b]Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]Run the game using SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]Requires Stardew Valley 1.6. Safe to add to an existing save, and safe to remove: your grabbers go back to vanilla behaviour and keep whatever they were holding. In multiplayer, collection is handled by the host.
[line]

[size=4][b]Troubleshooting[/b][/size]

Turn on [b]VerboseLogging[/b] and each pass reports itself. If something's broken, please include that log with your bug report.
[spoiler]
[code]Grabber at Farm (59, 20) | runs TenMinutes | scope Local -> Farm | grabs 2: Furnace, Heavy Tapper
    collected 6 in 13ms: Pine Tar x3, Oak Resin x1, Maple Syrup x1, Copper Bar x1
    passed over: Heavy Tapper: nothing ready to collect (x5)[/code]The [b]passed over[/b] line is usually the answer: a machine that hasn't finished, a clump needing a better tool, or an item dropped on the ground because the grabber was full.[/spoiler]

Downloads.Description: New Buildings group: fish ponds and mills can finally be collected from. Everything else here no longer ticks the rows below it, so it covers modded content only, and check all leaves it alone. Existing grabbers keep collecting what they collected.
